## 1256 N Artesian Ave — Zoning & Development Evaluation
**PIN: 16012280180000 | West Town (Community Area 24)**

---

### 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **RM-4.5** (Residential Multi-Unit), per the City's official GIS zoning system (Ordinance A7210). You can verify at the [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning).

---

### 2. Is Multi-Unit (3+ Units) Permitted by Right?

**Yes.** The RM-4.5 district expressly accommodates "multi-unit buildings" as a permitted use [4]. Three or more units are permitted by right — no special use or Planned Development is required at this scale. The lot area math (see §6 below) is the binding constraint, not use permission.

---

### 3. Key Bulk & Density Standards

All figures are from the zoning table for RM-4.5, per [2]:

| Standard | RM-4.5 Value |
|---|---|
| **FAR** | 1.7 |
| **Max height** | 45–47 ft (varies by lot frontage) |
| **Min lot area per dwelling unit** | 700 sq ft |
| **Min lot size** | 1,650 sq ft |
| **Side setbacks** | None required in RM districts between residential buildings; B/C-abutment rules differ [5] |

> **Important:** [2] explicitly cautions that these density standards "are not to be interpreted as a guarantee that allowed densities can be achieved on every lot — other factors, such as off-street parking, height limits, dwelling unit sizes and lot configuration may work to limit density more."

Efficiency and SRO units count at smaller lot-area thresholds than standard dwelling units, which can allow higher unit counts [2].

---

### 4. Overlays & Special Designations

- **ADU Eligible Area** [1]: This parcel is within a designated Additional Dwelling Unit–Allowed area, enabling legal development of ADUs (coach houses, conversion units) per [1]. Enforcement is by the Department of Housing at pre-certification.
- **Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone**: Development triggering ARO thresholds will require affordable unit set-asides or in-lieu fees. West Town has 20 ARO housing projects totaling 291 affordable units in the community area, reflecting active enforcement.
- **Special District**: The parcel is flagged as within a Special District overlay, though no specific ordinance number was provided in the retrieved data — verify the precise restrictions with the Department of Planning and Development (DPD).
- **No Planned Development** required at this scale.
- **No landmark, historic, or lakefront protection** designations apply.
- **Not in a Special Service Area (SSA).**
- **Transit-served:** The nearest CTA rail is the Damen Blue Line station (0.67 miles). The parcel is **not TOD-eligible** under the Connected Communities Ordinance, so no parking reduction or density bonus applies on that basis.
- **Flood Zone X** — Area of Minimal Flood Hazard; flood insurance is not required. No brownfield sites nearby.

---

### 5. Parking Requirement & Transit-Related Reduction

Off-street parking for residential uses in RM districts must be located on the same zoning lot as the dwelling units served [3]. Parking spaces are prohibited in side setbacks and within 20 feet of the front property line; they are permitted in a required side setback when accessed by a permitted driveway from the front [3].

**No transit-related parking reduction applies** — the parcel is not TOD-eligible, so the Connected Communities parking relief (§17-10-0102-B) does not apply here. You should confirm the specific per-unit parking minimums for RM-4.5 with DPD or the full parking table in §17-10-0200, as that table was not retrieved in this session.

---

### 6. Maximum Units by Right — Can You Build 6?

**By lot area alone: 4 units maximum. Six units is not achievable by right on this lot.**

The arithmetic from the zoning table [2]:
> 3,191 sq ft (parcel) ÷ 700 sq ft per unit = **4.56 → 4 units** (fractional units round down)

- **4 units** is the lot-area ceiling by right.
- **6 units would require ~4,200 sq ft** of lot area at 700 sq ft/unit — roughly 1,000 sq ft more than this parcel.
- Note that efficiency or SRO units count at smaller lot-area thresholds [2], so mixing unit types *could* push the count higher — but this would need confirmation against the full density table in §17-2-0303.
- FAR (1.7), height (45–47 ft), and parking requirements could further constrain achievable units even within the 4-unit ceiling.
- A **Planned Development** or **map amendment** to a higher RM class would be required to reach 6 units on this lot.

**To verify:** Pull the full §17-2-0303 density table and §17-10-0200 parking table from [Chicago's Municipal Code](https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/depts/dcd/supp_info/chicago_zoningordinance.html) or contact DPD's zoning counter at (312) 744-5777.

---

### Confidence & Limitations

| Item | Confidence | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| Zoning district | **High** — authoritative GIS match | — |
| Use permission (3+ units) | **High** | — |
| FAR, height, density | **High** — from zoning table | Lot coverage not in retrieved data |
| Unit yield (4 units) | **High** | Efficiency/SRO uplift needs full density table |
| Parking minimums | **Medium** | Per-unit rates not retrieved |
| Special District details | **Low** | No ordinance number in data; verify with DPD |
| 6-unit feasibility | **High (no)** — math is clear | PD/rezoning path not evaluated |

> This parcel is **city-owned** (Status: "Owned by City / Interest"), meaning acquisition would involve the City's land disposition process — contact DPD's land sales team before proceeding.
